posts.cooked:
I'm sure that all depends on what you want from your Bond.  Connery's got the 1960s misogynist charm, Moore's got the goofy/coolest gadgets, Brosnan's got the steely suaveness, and Craig's got blonde hair.

For me personally, Dalton is the worst (if you don't count Lazenby).  He never seemed cool and his movies are some of the boringest while simultaneously being the most outrageous (I'm sure it was quite a feat to get that semi-truck to go up on half its wheels to dodge a missile, but come on.  It's a truck dodging a missile).  Maybe it's just his bad luck to have been Bond during the '90s.

But you probably have just as subjective reasons for why you think Dalton's the best.  Bring them forth.

I'm not sure I've ever actually seen any of these movies, but based on clips and advertisements, I just can't really imagine any Bond other than Pierce Brosnan.  He just does the "suave secret agent" thing to perfection by my standards.  I'm glad that Daniel Craig got the new Bond movies though, because it probably led to him being cast as Lord Asriel in the Golden Compass movie, and I find it hard to imagine anyone else in that role.

Edit - The only other Bond I'm even slightly familiar with is Connery, and as with Brosnan, this is a product of me having grown up in the 90's...to me, Sean is a dignified old greybeard, not a slick youthful seducer.  He just looks wrong to me in all the Bond movies.  I accept that this is completely subjective and shallow of me.

posts.name: Hardboiledgregg
posts.cooked:
I liked Dalton as Bond. He got the short straw when it came to the films themselves, in some regards (though compared to a few others, there could be a long argument in favour of Licence to Kill). He had that sort of dangerous charm that Connery could sometimes exude. Problem was, I think he arrived at a time when 'gritty' was in, and that dates very quickly without some substance behind it.

Anyway, it'd be hard to replace Connery as the original, but I liked Brosnan (though his films were a bit hit-and-miss) and Craig makes a very good Bond for a new era. The character-focused story-telling and style of action is a refreshing change, and Craig carries it well. Though, I must say I was a little disappointed with Skyfall.

posts.name: danmarshall14
posts.cooked:
Casino Royale was an exciting movie and a great kickoff into Craig's "prequel" trilogy.  People complain that the movie didn't capture the full spirit of Bond, but I always argued it was because Casino was supposed to take place when Bond was still fresh as a 00 agent; that spirit of Bond didn't exist yet and what is left is something more raw than suave.  I thought it fit perfectly.

Quantum of Solace was, unfortunately, a product of the writers' strike that took place a handful of years ago; the production team basically admitted that fact, apologized, and promised that Skyfall would make up for it tenfold.  And they definitely delivered.

Overall, I have to say Craig is my favorite Bond.  I know the general population's opinion is eager to dismiss him, proposing that the classics are irreplacable.  But personally, I'm not that nostalgic.  I love Connery and Dalton; From Russia with Love is among my top movies of all time.  But, when I look at what the Craig trilogy accomplished (despite Quantum of Solace's shortcomings), I can't help but be completely enthralled with it.
